newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Qantas plans Boeing 747SPs for Melbourne-HK.
newsitem.headline: Qantas plans Boeing 747SPs for Melbourne-HK.

text.p: Qantas Airways is to replace Boeing 767-300 aircraft with Boeing 747-SPs on the Melbourne to Hong Kong route because of growing passenger demand, an airline executive told Reuters.

But the switch in April to the smallest version of the 747 family will mean a reduction in freight capacity. The Boeing SP or Special Performance aircraft has a belly cargo capacity of 28.8 tonnes compared with 34.2 tonnes in a 767-300, Qantas regional manager freight, Peter Barry said.
In a telephone interview from his Singapore headquarters, Barry said said the larger aircraft would enable more passengers to be carried on a very important route for the airline.

The Boeing SP can carry around 320 passengers compared to 228 on extended range Boeing 767-ERs used by Qantas. However he added that the reduction in freight capacity would have a minimal effect on cargo operations.

Barry said the Hong Kong-Melbourne route was having a "great" financial year. The cargo consisted mainly of produce exports from Australia with large amounts of garments and high value electronic goods -- made in China -- going back to Australia.

"Hong Kong is doing very well for us predominantly because the business levels coming out of China have gone very well. We have also been able to feed a certain level of traffic from Europe through Hong Kong," Barry said.
